Die Nacht im Kollektiv: The Night in the Collective (Die Nacht im Kollektiv)
Someone broke into Mara’s server. You read the logs like an investigator: who, when, how – and how do you prevent it?
Spuren in Logdateien finden und zu einer: Find traces in log files and put them together into a timeline. As a pentester, you then know exactly what traces your attacks leave behind.
Nur die gesicherten Logs in der Sandbox: Only the saved logs in the sandbox (~/spuren). Made-up case.
Spurensicherung · Sandbox bereit. Start:: Evidence collection · Sandbox ready. Start: cat LIESMICH.txt
Brute-Force, Web-Scan, offene Sicherung,: Brute force, web scan, exposed backup, login as backup, looking around, leaving a message.
Ein Angriff ist eine Kette. Logs machen: An attack is a chain. Logs make it visible – and every countermeasure should close the real gap, not just a symptom.
Echte Logs sind riesig und unordentlich;: Real logs are huge and messy; professionals use tools like SIEM systems for them. The way of thinking is the same.
Probier es in Kali: journalctl und /var/: Try it in Kali: journalctl and /var/log show you the traces of your own exercises (e.g. from the Kellerserver: docker logs kly-keller).
Was die Webseite verrät: Was die Webseite verrät (what the website gives away)
Heute Nacht war jemand auf unserem Serve: Tonight someone was on our server "kollektiv". I saved the logs:
logs/verlauf.txt – Befehle, die im Ko: logs/verlauf.txt  – commands typed in the account "backup"
Finde heraus: Wer war es, wie kam er rei: Find out: who was it, how did they get in, what did they do – and how do we prevent it?
(Alles erfunden. Die IP-Adressen stammen: (All made up. The IP addresses come from ranges that are reserved for examples only.)
Gruss an das Kollektiv. Eure Sicherung l: Greetings to the Collective. Your backup was lying open on the net. {code}
Fang bei den Anmeldungen an. Fehlgeschla: Start with the logins. Failed logins are called "Failed password" in auth.log.
Von welcher IP kamen die meisten fehlges: Which IP did most failed logins come from?
grep \"Failed password\" logs/auth.log z: grep "Failed password" logs/auth.log shows all failed attempts. The IP comes after "from".
Mit sed schneidest du alles bis „from “: With sed you cut away everything up to "from ": sed 's/.* from //'. Then the IP is at the front – cut -d' ' -f1 takes only that.
Lösung: grep Failed logs/auth.log | sed: Solution: grep Failed logs/auth.log | sed 's/.* from //' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr → 203.0.113.77
Wie viele Fehlversuche kamen von dieser: How many failed attempts came from this IP?
grep kann mit -c zählen. Kombiniere zwei: grep can count with -c. Combine two conditions with a pipe.
Wie nennt man so einen Angriff?: What is an attack like this called?
Brute-Force: sehr viele Passwörter für v: Brute force: trying a great many passwords for different users.
143 Versuche in rund 35 Minuten, verschi: 143 attempts in about 35 minutes, different user names …
Irgendwann hat es geklappt. Erfolgreiche: At some point it worked. Successful logins are called "Accepted".
Mit welchem Benutzerkonto kam der Angrei: Which user account did the attacker get in with?
grep Accepted logs/auth.log – aber nur d: grep Accepted logs/auth.log – but only the line with the attacker’s IP.
Lösung: grep Accepted logs/auth.log | gr: Solution: grep Accepted logs/auth.log | grep 203.0.113.77 → backup
Die Uhrzeit steht am Anfang derselben Ze: The time is at the start of the same line.
Mara meldet sich mit „publickey“ an, der: Mara logs in with "publickey", the attacker with "password". What follows from that?
Hätte der Server nur Schlüssel erlaubt (: If the server had allowed only keys (no password login), the password alone would have been useless.
Kann man einen SSH-Schlüssel erraten wie: Can you guess an SSH key like a password?
Woher kannte der Angreifer das richtige: How did the attacker know the right password? Maybe they browsed around the website first.
Welches Scan-Werkzeug verrät sich im Use: Which scanning tool gives itself away in the user agent?
grep 203.0.113.77 logs/access.log – der: grep 203.0.113.77 logs/access.log – the user agent is at the very end in quotation marks.
Welche Datei hat er erfolgreich herunter: Which file did they download successfully? (path)
Erfolgreich heißt Status 200. Der Status: Successful means status 200. The status comes right after the part in quotation marks.
Große Downloads erkennst du an der Größe: You recognize big downloads by the size after the status.
Eine Sicherung lag offen auf der Webseit: A backup was lying open on the website. It probably contained the password of the account backup – the brute force came first, the hit afterwards.
Der Angreifer hat das Passwort erraten,: The attacker guessed the password, the file does not matter.
Vergleiche die Uhrzeiten: Download um 02: Compare the times: download at 02:38, login at 02:41.
Der Verlauf im Konto backup zeigt die ge: The history in the account backup shows the typed commands.
Was hat der Angreifer nach dem Login vor: What did the attacker mainly do after logging in?
Sich umgesehen: wer er ist, welche Benut: Looked around: who they are, which users exist, whether they can get more permissions (sudo -l, files with special permissions, cron jobs).
Lies logs/verlauf.txt Zeile für Zeile. W: Read logs/verlauf.txt line by line. Which commands do you know from the Kellerserver?
Er hat eine Nachricht hinterlassen. Flag: They left a message. Flag from it
Eine Zeile im Verlauf schreibt etwas Cod: One line in the history writes something encoded to /tmp/.gruss.
Der Text zwischen den Anführungszeichen: The text between the quotation marks is base64.
Lösung: grep gruss logs/verlauf.txt | cu: Solution: grep gruss logs/verlauf.txt | cut -d'"' -f2 | base64 -d
Die letzte Zeile ist „history -c“. Warum: The last line is "history -c". Why is the history still there?
The history was saved before or logged separately – covering tracks rarely works completely.
Wer hat die Datei gesichert, und wann?: Who saved the file, and when?
Put everything together and advise Mara.
Brute-Force startet (02:05) → Web-Scan m: Brute force starts (02:05) → web scan with Nikto (02:20) → download of the backup (02:38) → login as backup (02:41) → looking around → logout (03:02)
Sort the times from both logs.
Passwort von backup ändern und Passwort-: Change the password of backup and switch off password login via SSH, remove the backup from the web server, check whether other accounts are affected.
Die IP 203.0.113.77 sperren – das reicht: Block the IP 203.0.113.77 – that is enough.
Nothing, they did not delete anything.
Eine einzelne IP zu sperren hilft wenig: Blocking a single IP helps little – the attacker can use another one. What is the real gap?
Was lernst du als Pentester daraus?: What do you learn from this as a pentester?
Jeder Scan, jeder Login-Versuch und jede: Every scan, every login attempt and every command leaves traces – that is why you only work with an assignment and document everything.
